title: Resumable HTTP streaming: hybrid chunk-framing + resume-window protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a hybrid resumable streaming protocol for HTTP-based responses that preserves compatibility with older clients while providing deterministic chunk framing, resume semantics, and safety for structured/function-call payloads. Goal is to reduce failed partial responses during transient network issues, avoid duplicate tool invocations, and make server-side recovery predictable.
acceptance_criteria: Client can request a resume-enabled stream via Accept: application/x-redwood-resumable+json or query param ?resume=1
Server emits framed chunks with stable chunk IDs and optional resume tokens (resume token included at least every N bytes/event boundaries)
On reconnect the client can supply last-seen chunk id and resume token and server resumes without re-executing side-effectful tool calls
Fallback: older clients that do not negotiate resumable mode receive a backwards-compatible SSE/plain-chunk stream
Automated tests validate no duplicate function/tool-call invocations across network reconnects for at least 99.9% of cases in integration harness
Telemetry surfaces resume success rate, duplicate-invocation rate, and bytes-resumed histogram
implementation_notes: Protocol: stream frames are JSON objects separated by a single newline. Each frame includes: 'chunk_id' (monotonic), 'offset_bytes', 'type' (data|meta|heartbeat|call_confirm), 'payload' (string or base64 if binary), and optional 'resume_token' at configurable intervals
Resume negotiation: client sends header X-RW-Resume: v1 or query param; servers respond with X-RW-Resume-Enabled: true/false
Chunk id semantics: chunk_id is globally unique per stream and idempotent on replay. Server must persist minimal in-flight mapping until resume window expires (configurable, default 60s).

Tool/function calls: side-effectful call events are marked with type 'call_confirm' and include a stable 'call_id'. Server guarantees at-least-once delivery to downstream tools internally but exposes an idempotency layer that will not re-issue calls for the same call_id during resume window

Backpressure: prefer HTTP/2 stream flow-control and map to runtime batching; if client is slow use continuous-batching to limit memory growth and emit 'backpressure' meta frames when thresholds crossed

Compatibility: older SSE clients receive Content-Type: text/event-stream fallback with data: lines that embed the same JSON per event. New clients get application/x-redwood-resumable+json with framed lines. Server must support both on same endpoint via content-negotiation
Security: resume tokens encode stream checksum and timestamp and are HMAC'd with server key to prevent token forging; token rotation supported via versioned secrets

KV cache interactions: when resuming a stream with cached prefix, ensure the resumed token includes model kv-version to validate cache consistency; if mismatch, server should return a non-resumable error instructing client to restart from scratch
Edge considerations: proxies may buffer; include periodic heartbeat frames (type 'heartbeat') to keep connections alive; recommend heartbeat every 15s for long-lived streams
Metrics: add counters for resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fail_reason, duplicate_call_detected, frames_emitted, average_resume_bytes
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement resumable negotiation and server-side framing behind feature flag for 5% of hosted traffic
Phase 2 (SDKs): update JS/Go/Python SDKs to negotiate resumable streams and provide client helper to persist last-seen chunk metadata
Phase 3 (rollout): increase rollout to 50% after 1 week of stable absence of duplicate-call anomalies, then 100% after SDK adoption metrics reach 80%
Phase 4 (deprecation): keep text/event-stream fallback for 6 months after full rollout, then evaluate removal depending on client compatibility telemetry
qa_tests: Network flakiness injection: force TCP drops at random intervals and verify client resumes correctly using last-seen chunk_id/token
Tool idempotency: simulate function-call side effect and assert no duplicate downstream side effects after server resume
Compatibility checks: old SSE-only SDK should still receive and parse events without errors
KV mismatch scenario: validate server returns non-resumable error with clear client-retry guidance when model/kv state diverges
Load tests: ensure resume token persistence does not materially increase memory under 10k concurrent resumable streams per runtime shard
rollout_steps: Create feature-flag gate 'resumable_streaming_v1' in infra and add to canary cluster
Merge runtime patch selecting framing format and token emission frequency (configurable flag 'resume_emit_interval_bytes')
Publish SDK updates with automatic resume helper and sample code in docs
Run 72h canary monitoring dashboard and set automatic rollback on duplicate_call_rate > 0.1%
Enable for Dedicated tenants on request and include admin toggle in Console
notes: Design trade-off: emitting resume_token on every chunk simplifies clients but increases bandwidth; our hybrid design emits token at event boundaries and every ~64KB by default

We must be conservative around call_confirm ordering: if a data frame with function args is emitted and the next frame is call_confirm, client libraries must not re-issue call if they reconnect prior to call_confirm re-delivery
Consider future extension to support consumer ACK frames for strict at-most-once semantics when downstream systems expose idempotency keys
Follow-up ticket: add server admin endpoint to inspect recent resumable token validity windows for forensic/debugging (ENG-17902)
Docs: include migration guide for self-hosted/private customers that use proxies which might terminate keepalives
